items.summary: The Iran SNSC determination on the Hormuz re-closure remains unannounced through Saturday evening — Day 9 of contested compliance and the second full day since the Majlis ratification confirmed the SNSC as the formal decision node. The re-closure is formally operative. The IRGC cargo ship strike confirmed in the June 26 morning brief — four one-way attack drones launched, one impacting the upper deck of an IMO-backed cargo vessel on the Oman corridor route — remains entirely unaddressed by the SNSC: no attribution acknowledgment, no disciplinary framing, no re-closure retraction. The IMO has paused the 118-tanker evacuation convoy framework following the strike. The SNSC's extended silence through Day 9 is increasingly difficult to read as procedural delay: two days after Majlis ratification, with Lebanon surpassing all ceasefire durability thresholds, the absence of an announcement reflects either acute internal factional division between IRGC-aligned hardliners and Pezeshkian pragmatists, or deliberate strategic ambiguity intended to extract additional concessions from the Swiss technical framework. Either interpretation is structurally negative for the pump-relief chain. Lebanon ceasefire advanced to Hour ~124+ through Saturday without a formal void declaration. Secretary Rubio's framework announcement (June 26) — Hezbollah to end hostilities and withdraw from southern Lebanon; Israel commits not to target Beirut's southern suburbs; establishment of pilot coordination zones — represents the most significant diplomatic layering since the MOU signing and provides new scaffolding for the SNSC's re-closure justification. However, Netanyahu's explicit and repeated refusal to set a withdrawal timeline from the southern Lebanon security buffer zone ('we will stay as long as necessary'; IDF occupying 570 km²) remains the primary structural constraint: the SNSC cannot credibly frame a retraction as conditional on Lebanese-front resolution while Israeli forces hold the buffer without a phased withdrawal commitment. WTI settled at $69.40 on Friday (Saturday markets closed) — Day 6 below the $74 normalization-confidence floor and a 3.51% daily decline. The market continues front-running an SNSC announcement that has not materialized; sub-$70 WTI while 118 tankers remain commercially stranded and Lloyd's war-risk premiums hold at 3-8% (vs. 0.25% pre-conflict) reflects supply-positive anticipation the compliance framework does not yet support. If the SNSC does not announce through the weekend, the front-running gap creates a reversion risk for Monday's opening. Oregon pump prices approximately $5.35/gallon; national approximately $4.56/gallon.

items.summary: Secondary geopolitical developments carry elevated structural weight on June 27. North Korea: Kim Jong Un attended commissioning of the Choe Hyon on June 23 — North Korea's first 5,000-tonne destroyer, a significant milestone in Kim's stated objective to equip the navy with nuclear weapons. On June 25, Kim oversaw weapons tests evaluated as a 'deadly and destructive offensive posture': a 'special mission' warhead for tactical ballistic missiles, upgraded multiple rocket launch systems, and an extended-range self-propelled gun-howitzer. South Korea's Defense Ministry announced plans to expand drone forces in direct response. US-China: China's Ministry of Finance announced an immediate ban on PRC government entities purchasing from 46 US companies, including Lockheed Martin and Raytheon — targeted defense-sector economic retaliation linked to US arms posture toward Taiwan. Chinese Coast Guard vessels have patrolled east of Taiwan nearly continuously since June 1; PRC carrier Liaoning returned to Qingdao June 23 after 40+ days deployed in the South China Sea and West Pacific. A Trump-Xi summit occurred covering global flashpoints; no major agreements on Iran or Taiwan were reached. Ukraine: Russia launched approximately 509 drones and missiles in recent operations, with at least 11 killed in Kharkiv strikes. Russia's 2026 escalation trajectory — 74 ballistic missiles/month (up from 49 in 2025), 75,000+ guided glide bombs projected for 2026 (vs. 60,000 in 2025) — reflects structural intensification. Ukrainian counter-strikes on Moscow have intensified sharply: nearly 40 drone strike events May 1-June 19, 2026 (vs. 4/month average in 2025), including multiple strikes on the Moscow Oil Refinery (June 15 and June 18). Crimea implemented emergency fuel restrictions following Ukrainian infrastructure strikes. Colombia escrutinio Day 8: De La Espriella 0.95-point preconteo lead holding without a disqualifying irregularity finding; certification projected within days; inauguration August 7. Peru ONPE Day 23: 50.10%/49.90% working count uncertified; full official count expected early July. Acting DNI vacancy advances to Day 38.

items.summary: WTI crude settled at $69.40 Friday — a 3.51% decline and Day 6 below the $74 normalization-confidence floor. The continued descent reflects market front-running of an SNSC announcement that has not been made: supply-positive sentiment driven by anticipation that the formal re-closure retraction is imminent and the 118-tanker backlog will begin clearing. The structural reversion risk on this front-running is now at its widest point in the brief cycle: 118 commercial tankers remain stranded; Lloyd's war-risk premiums hold at 3-8% of vessel value vs. 0.25% pre-conflict; the IMO convoy evacuation framework is paused following the IRGC strike; and the SNSC has not announced through Saturday. A Monday WTI opening reversion — if the weekend produces no SNSC announcement — would represent the supply-positive narrative's first significant challenge. Oregon pump approximately $5.35/gallon; national approximately $4.56/gallon; pump relief remains fully gated on the SNSC-to-Lloyd's-to-backlog-to-supply-pulse chain. US equity markets closed the week in broad retreat, with technology underperforming sharply: S&P 500 -2.0% for the week (Friday close 7,354.02, -0.05% daily); Nasdaq -4.6% for the week (Friday close 25,297.62, -0.24% daily; fifth consecutive losing session); Dow outperformed at +0.6% weekly. Two AI-sector concerns drove the tech sell-off: OpenAI's reported decision to delay its IPO to 2027 weighed on AI-adjacent sentiment broadly; investor anxiety about escalating AI data center infrastructure costs prompted rotation out of high-multiple technology names into defensive sectors. The AI capex anxiety is structurally linked to the FERC large-load show-cause orders (Day 11): the acceleration of data center power demand driving the regulatory inquiry is the same force testing ROI assumptions in the equity market. FOMC holds at 3.50-3.75% (June 17 decision). Kevin Warsh's first meeting as Chair removed forward guidance language implying a cut-bias — a hawkish signal validated by May CPI (4.2% annual, May PCE 4.1% annual). Markets now price a potential rate hike as early as October 2026. Nine FOMC hike-dots remain operative. June CPI releases July 14.

Ground crews completed final consolidation of the remaining 5% uncontained perimeter under favorable overnight conditions. The declaration eliminates the compounding-resource-demand risk that defined the June 22-24 escalation: all PNW fire suppression resources — aerial and ground — are now available for new onset-period ignitions beginning June 28, with no active under-contained fire competing for assets. The East Cascades onset window arrives T-1; new season ignitions are expected as the seasonal high-pressure rebuilds through late June and early July, but the resource baseline entering onset is the strongest of the brief cycle. NSF Newport OR continues operational per the Friday Trump administration reversal and unanimous Senate block — the coastal atmospheric anchor for fire-weather modeling enters the onset window intact. BPA grid is stable Day 8 post-heat-advisory with no forced outages. NIFC PL3 Day 11. Oregon EO 26-10 Day 14: 414 fires and approximately 8,000+ acres YTD. Secondary Washington large fires at near-resolution: Tule Road approximately 97%, Juniper Dunes approximately 93%, Upriver in final mop-up. Active PNW fires generating smoke in eastern Washington and Oregon include the Garred Road and Lytle fires; burn bans in effect across multiple counties. National 2026 YTD context: approximately 2.6 million acres burned, nearly double the 2025 pace; above-average significant wildfire potential forecast for the entire PNW through September 2026, with comparisons drawn to the 2015 season (worst in regional history).

CISA guidance requires critical infrastructure to develop offline operational capabilities for prolonged internet and telecom outages — a posture that reflects the ODNI 2026 Annual Threat Assessment's warning of escalating cyber challenges to the energy sector. The North American Electric Reliability Corporation reports the US grid acquires approximately 60 new vulnerable points daily from accelerating digitalization, distributed energy resource integration, and third-party vendor dependencies. Iran and IRGC-affiliated groups are identified as elevated threat vectors. The IRGC cargo ship strike and SNSC non-announcement represent a deterioration of the implicit constraint that the MOU's diplomatic track placed on IRGC cyber operations targeting US energy infrastructure — the 'post-MOU IRGC cyber window' is now assessed as more open than at any point in the compliance period. The AI capex acceleration driving both the FERC orders and the equity market sell-off is the grid's most acute medium-term structural challenge — data center power demand curves are outpacing transmission capacity buildout by an estimated 3-5 years. FEMA announced $420 million in emergency management grants (opened June 15): $337 million for Emergency Management Performance Grants to states, local, and tribal governments; $83 million for Emergency Operations Center construction and upgrade. Water infrastructure authorization expires September 30, 2026; over 60% of US utilities are operating beyond intended lifespan.

At 54% of normal, BPA hydroelectric generation capacity is structurally compromised, creating an electricity cost premium that compounds the AI data center demand surge and the Hormuz energy-price backdrop. Washington drought emergency advances to Day 25 — fourth consecutive drought year, 12 emergency counties, 50% statewide snowpack vs. normal, 23 reservoir systems below historical averages. Super El Niño watch continues at 25% probability (KLCC/OPB June 22); base El Niño probability approximately 61%. A Super El Niño in 2026-2027 would produce a fifth consecutive critically dry, warm PNW drought winter — the single most consequential long-range risk factor in the regional portfolio. ENSO monitoring update expected early July. L-Pod orca calf continues alive entering Week 5 — a continued positive signal for the critically endangered Southern Resident Killer Whale population under sustained fisheries and Chinook stress. Oregon's 21st gray whale washup of 2026 (near Lincoln City) is the marine mammal stress indicator. Echinococcus multilocularis peri-urban surveillance in Washington coyote populations: no new confirmed spread events Saturday.
